newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi index down on low activity.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi index down on low activity.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index continued on a downward trend on Wednesday, dragged by losses and low activity in a market focused on a primary issue by Kenya Commercial Bank, brokers said.
The index fell 18.27 points to stand at 3023.34 points. Turnover was posted at 7.562 million shillings compared to 37.667 million shillings on Tuesday.
A senior broker said the market was generally down. Most investors were adopting a wait-and-see attitude to see if the market would turn around, "as in prices will start to pick up."
A bourse official said activity was low compared to Tuesday. He saw high Tuesday turnover as influenced by big lots traded on the special board.
"There are some factors that are undermining the market at present and Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB) sale of 11.88 primary share is one of them," a broker said.
Most investors seemed to be getting out of their current counters to take advantage of the KCB shares, the broker said.
Housing Finance Company and National Bank of Kenya, which had been leading the market's trading for the last three weeks, were down in thin volumes.
Housing Finance eased to 23.75 from 25.25, National Bank of Kenya traded 31,200 shares at 16.70, 16.40 and 16.65 from 17 and Kenya Commercial Bank dropped 2.50 shillings to 52.50.
Most plantations held steady; Rea Vipingo at 11, Brooke Bond at 177 while Sasini Tea & Coffee fell 1.0 to 49.
Car & General fell to 20.50 from 21.50, Kenya Airways traded 77,689 shares at 11, 10 and 10.10 from 10.55, Marshalls East Africa Ltd eased to 46 from 47.
Oil Concern Total Kenya fell 3.0 shillings to 70.
Official said all was quite on the foreign investors board.
